baseline.note: Gold v0.2 acceptance is closed and not reopened by this audit. This audit is orthogonal: it evaluates live-serving/UI/UX demo readiness, not detection-semantics correctness.

startup.backend: console script `comqutor-api` (pyproject.toml) -> uvicorn on 127.0.0.1:8000 by default (never 0.0.0.0). Requires COMQUTOR_CORS_ORIGINS set explicitly (no wildcard allowed) for the frontend origin to be permitted. Falls back to local SQLite if COMQUTOR_DATABASE_URL unset (dev only).
startup.frontend: Vite dev server fixed at 127.0.0.1:5175 (`npm run dev` in frontend/), redirects `/` to `/research`.
startup.live_execution_gate: COMQUTOR_REAL_TRADINGAGENTS_ENABLED / COMQUTOR_WEEK2_LLM_ENABLED must be explicitly enabled (operator shell only, never .env) for a real live research run; scripts/start_live_comqutor.sh is the privileged launcher.
startup.no_combined_docker_service: docker-compose.yml only defines the upstream TradingAgents CLI container and an optional postgres profile -- there is no COMQUTOR API/frontend Docker service today.

terminal_manual_intervention_points: Enabling COMQUTOR_REAL_TRADINGAGENTS_ENABLED/COMQUTOR_WEEK2_LLM_ENABLED requires an operator shell, cannot be toggled from the UI (by design, for cost/safety control).

No discoverable UI affordance today to reliably 'load a known-good persisted run' for a demo -- a presenter would need to know a run_id and navigate to /runs/<run_id>/research directly, or use the Recent Runs table on /research (exists, but not framed as a demo tool).

frontend.framework: React 18.3.1 + TypeScript 5.6.3 (strict) + Vite 5.4.8, react-router-dom 6.26.2, no UI component library (hand-written CSS)
frontend.state_management: No global store; local component state + small custom hooks (useResearchSubmission, useRunPolling, useResearchRun); cross-page continuity via run_id in the URL
frontend.api_client: frontend/src/api/client.ts; base URL from VITE_COMQUTOR_API_BASE_URL, defaults to same-origin; no hardcoded localhost found in src/; every response validated through adapters.ts before use (never a bare `as Type` cast)
frontend.loading_ux: GOOD -- LoadingPanel spinner, real backend-driven progress bar + percent + ETA range + elapsed time + ordered stage checklist (ProcessingPage.tsx); polling via useRunPolling with [1000,2000,3000,5000]ms backoff
frontend.error_ux: GOOD -- centralized ApiError type, curated safe copy table (KNOWN_ERROR_CODE_MESSAGES), ErrorPanel never renders raw error objects/stack traces/JSON; one minor nuance: ApiError.contractMismatch() message includes a dev-facing instruction ('Check VITE_COMQUTOR_API_BASE_URL and restart the frontend') that could confuse a non-technical demo viewer if the API base URL is ever misconfigured live
frontend.debug_admin_views: No gated debug/admin route exists. ReplayAllPanel ('Reprocess saved outputs', triggers POST /api/replay-all) is embedded directly on the public /research landing page for every visitor with no access-control gate beyond a confirm dialog -- an operator-flavored batch action visible to any demo viewer.
frontend.responsive: Multiple breakpoints (640px/768px/1024px), dark-mode support, prefers-reduced-motion support, e2e test asserting no horizontal overflow -- genuine responsive intent
frontend.security_sanity: No hardcoded localhost/secrets/absolute paths in src/. One minor internal-detail leak: literal relative path 'outputs/runs/' appears in ReplayAllPanel copy. ReplayAllPanel's unguarded public exposure is the main demo-sanity flag (not a security vulnerability -- it makes 0 Provider/TradingAgents calls -- but a UX/accidental-trigger risk during a live demo).

backend_api.entry_point: POST /api/research (comqutor_alpha/api/routes_research.py) -- async job-queue model, returns {run_id,status,cache_disposition,...} immediately (200 reused-completed / 202 created-or-running / mapped 4xx-5xx for config/validation errors), pipeline runs in background never on the request thread
backend_api.status_polling: GET /api/research/{run_id}/status -- DB-only read, rich contract: progress_percent, current_stage, completed_units/total_units, elapsed_seconds, eta_status + estimated_remaining_seconds_min/max, progress_message (curated safe copy, never raw exception text)
backend_api.final_result: GET /api/research/{run_id} -- full canonical response (dominant_alphas, main_conflict, summary, entity_alpha_exposures, data_sanity_*, evidence_stance_summary, alpha_memory, unclassified_findings_*); status only becomes 'completed' if graph+conflict+ticker_consistency+artifact_completeness all pass, otherwise fail-closed to 'partial'
backend_api.alpha_library_endpoint: GET /api/alpha-library and /api/alpha-library/{alpha_id} DO expose the full ID->human-name(name_en/name_cn)+core_thesis+invalidation_conditions+conflict_alphas mapping to any API client -- the human-readable-name translation layer already exists at the API boundary, it is not merely a docs/audit-artifact convenience
backend_api.provider_reliability_exposure: Provider timeout/retry/validation-failure/fallback counts (per Step 7B.3's authoritative Provider-Health figures: 617 requests, 25 timeouts, 9 validation failures, 34 recoverable semantic-critical events, 0 fatal failures) are recorded only in an internal, non-API-exposed sidecar (llm_semantic_calls.jsonl / llm_semantic_manifest.json) -- never reachable via any public route, not even the generic artifact-download route (not in the download allowlist). A normal API client/demo viewer has zero visibility into retry noise -- by construction, not by UI-layer filtering.
backend_api.security_sanity: No hardcoded absolute local paths in comqutor_alpha/api/*.py; explicit _UNSAFE_DATA_SANITY_DETAIL_MARKERS scrubber strips path/credential/traceback-shaped substrings from any data_sanity warning before it reaches a client; no debug=True on the FastAPI app; .env files correctly gitignored and untracked; CORS defaults to no middleware at all unless explicitly configured, wildcard '*' is rejected at startup.

critical_finding_db_availability_gap.description: Empirically confirmed during this audit (read-only GET calls against already-persisted data, no Provider/TradingAgents calls): the QQQ post-fix run f239a53f-4ebe-455c-bb76-5f5485903901 has complete, rich file artifacts on disk (structure_graph.json, conflicts.json, run_audit.json all present and internally consistent) but its rows are MISSING from the current outputs/runs/_comqutor_alpha_graph.db. Because /status, /graph, and /conflicts are DB-only reads with no file-artifact fallback (by current design), calling them against this run_id returns RUN_STATUS_NOT_FOUND / GRAPH_NOT_READY / CONFLICTS_NOT_READY, and GET /api/research/{run_id} itself downgrades to status='partial', conflict_status='not_ready', dominant_alphas=[], main_conflict=null.
critical_finding_db_availability_gap.scope_unknown: Not verified in this pass whether NVDA (57d7b4c4-...) and SNDK (e8e0f398-...) have the same DB-row gap -- this must be checked before selecting final demo run_ids.
critical_finding_db_availability_gap.not_a_gold_acceptance_issue: This does not affect Gold v0.2 acceptance validity in any way -- Gold's authoritative source is the persisted file artifacts (run_audit.json), read directly, exactly as this entire acceptance process has done throughout. It is purely a live-API/demo-serving concern.

backend_api.manifest_inconsistency_minor_finding: llm_semantic_manifest.json for the QQQ post-fix run reports complete:false/finalized_at:null despite week3_pipeline_status.json reporting outcome:success and run_audit.json reporting PASS_WITH_WARNINGS -- not user-visible today (this file isn't API-exposed), but worth root-causing.

LIVE_FULL_RESEARCH.pros: most impressive/credible if it works flawlessly ('watch it think in real time')
LIVE_FULL_RESEARCH.cons: ~52 minutes wall clock for QQQ-scale runs; ~39 minutes of that shows one static stage message; nonzero Provider timeout/retry risk (25 timeouts / 9 validation failures observed even in a successful run) with zero visibility into recovery, could look like nothing is happening
LIVE_FULL_RESEARCH.credibility: HIGH if it succeeds, LOW if it times out or looks frozen mid-demo
LIVE_FULL_RESEARCH.failure_risk: HIGH for a live stakeholder setting
LIVE_FULL_RESEARCH.recommended_use: NOT recommended as the primary path for a time-boxed stakeholder demo; fine for a technical deep-dive session with time to spare

PERSISTED_RUN_DEMO.pros: instant, zero Provider/TradingAgents cost, zero timeout risk, fully reproducible/rehearsable
PERSISTED_RUN_DEMO.cons: not 'live' -- a skeptical viewer may ask to see a fresh ticker; currently blocked for at least one candidate run_id by the DB-availability gap found in this audit
PERSISTED_RUN_DEMO.implementation_complexity: LOW once the DB-availability gap is resolved for the chosen run_ids -- the routing/URL/component model already supports loading any completed run_id directly (/runs/:runId/research etc.)
PERSISTED_RUN_DEMO.credibility: MEDIUM-HIGH if framed honestly as 'a completed run we ran earlier'
PERSISTED_RUN_DEMO.failure_risk: LOW, contingent on the P0 DB-availability fix
PERSISTED_RUN_DEMO.recommended_use: RECOMMENDED as the backbone of the stakeholder demo

HYBRID_DEMO.pros: shows a rich, rehearsed result immediately (credibility + speed) while still offering to run a fresh ticker live if time/interest allows
HYBRID_DEMO.cons: slightly more presenter choreography; still inherits LIVE_FULL_RESEARCH's latency/risk if the live option is actually exercised
HYBRID_DEMO.implementation_complexity: LOW-MEDIUM -- mostly a presentation/product-framing decision on top of already-existing persisted-run loading + submission flows
HYBRID_DEMO.credibility: HIGH -- offers both instant proof and an optional live proof-point
HYBRID_DEMO.latency: instant for the primary story, ~52 min if the optional live path is taken
HYBRID_DEMO.failure_risk: LOW for the primary path, HIGH only if the optional live path is exercised and something goes wrong
HYBRID_DEMO.recommended_use: RECOMMENDED -- best overall balance: lead with PERSISTED_RUN_DEMO, offer a live run only as an optional closer with an explicit 'this will take about 50 minutes' expectation set up front

PRIMARY_DEMO_TICKER.why: Richest, clearest structural story: dominant Alpha (A301 Revenue Expansion, 78.49), 4 other active Alphas (A101 AI Expansion capped-active, A601 Narrative Momentum, A304 Multiple Compression, A103 AI Infrastructure), 3 admitted conflicts with a clear main conflict (A101__A304, bull-AI-thesis vs bear-valuation-risk), full evidence traceability. Formal Gold PASS (historical + impact-proof). Not chosen for being 'bullish' -- chosen because it has the most complete, legible structure/conflict/evidence story of the three inspected tickers.

SECONDARY_DEMO_TICKER.why: Demonstrates a genuinely different state (no dominant Alpha, 4 active Alphas including a capped/blocked one) plus a real, legitimate admitted conflict (A301__A304). Also carries the product's own remediation story (A001 false-positive fixed, now correctly non-detected) if a deeper technical narrative is wanted. Classified USABLE_WITH_CAVEAT (see Section 18) pending: (a) resolving the DB-availability gap for this specific run_id, and (b) disclosing the A301-evidence-strength REVIEW diagnostic if a technical stakeholder probes the conflict.

EDGE_CASE_DEMO_TICKER.why: The only inspected run with a dominant Alpha (A201 Semiconductor Supercycle, 84.22) but ZERO admitted conflicts (all 3 candidate pairs suppressed, main_conflict_id: null) -- a genuinely different, legitimate product state that is valuable to show deliberately (per Section 17's guidance not to assume every ticker has a dominant Alpha or a main conflict) rather than avoid. Also demonstrates a different Alpha family (semiconductor cycle) for taxonomy variety.

P0.problem: The QQQ post-fix run (f239a53f-...) has complete file artifacts but is missing DB rows, causing the live API to report RUN_STATUS_NOT_FOUND/GRAPH_NOT_READY/CONFLICTS_NOT_READY and the UI to show it as 'partial' with no conflict/dominant-Alpha data -- despite the underlying data being rich and correct.
P0.user_impact: If this exact run_id is opened live in the UI during a demo, it will appear broken even though nothing is actually wrong with the research result.
likely_files_modules: DB layer / research_runs, structure_graphs, alpha_conflicts tables
possibly a new 'reindex artifacts into DB' utility
P0.estimated_scope: SMALL_TO_MEDIUM (depends on whether a resync/backfill utility already exists)

P0.problem: Whichever run_ids are ultimately chosen for the stakeholder demo have not all been verified live-servable (only QQQ was directly checked in this audit and found broken; NVDA/SNDK are unverified).
P0.user_impact: A demo could break live if the presenter picks a run_id that also has this gap.
P0.estimated_scope: SMALL (a quick GET /status + /graph + /conflicts check against each candidate run_id before demo day)

P1.problem: The core 'what does the system see and why' story (Alpha list, dominant Alpha, main conflict) is split across three separate tabs (Research / Structure Graph / Conflict Radar) instead of appearing on the primary results page.
P1.user_impact: A demo viewer's first impression after a run completes is just a text summary -- they must know to click through tabs to see the actual structural findings.

P1.problem: Internal jargon (regime_level, candidate, 'B2 Conflict Evidence Admissibility gate', raw reason codes inline, Alpha Memory/SHADOW/phi_id) is shown in the default view without translation, contradicting the stated demo persona (non-engineer stakeholder).
P1.user_impact: A stakeholder sees confusing internal vocabulary during a normal (non-advanced) view of results.

P1.problem: No single, prominent 'research only, not financial advice' disclaimer -- only scattered, implicit copy.
P1.user_impact: Positioning risk if a stakeholder or downstream audience mistakes output for investment advice.

P1.problem: ReplayAllPanel (batch operator action) is exposed unguarded on the public /research landing page.
P1.user_impact: Could be confused with, or accidentally triggered during, a stakeholder demo.

P1.problem: Confidence/uncertainty is scattered across many small per-claim percentages with no single aggregate 'how sure is the system' indicator.
P1.user_impact: Harder for a viewer to quickly gauge overall confidence in the thesis.
P1.semantic_risk: LOW -- must remain a pure display statistic, never feed back into Gold detection thresholds

P1.problem: llm_semantic_manifest.json reports complete:false/finalized_at:null on the QQQ post-fix run despite the run succeeding overall.
P1.user_impact: Not user-visible today, but an unresolved internal inconsistency worth root-causing before it is ever surfaced.

P2.problem: The approved Invalidation Conditions registry only has one entry (A101); every other Alpha shows the honest 'not yet defined' fallback.
P2.user_impact: Limits what the Invalidation section can show for tickers/Alphas outside A101's family.
P2.backend_frontend_both: backend (content, requires human/product sign-off per entry, same discipline as A101's)
P2.semantic_risk: LOW -- adding approved content doesn't change scoring, but must follow the same approval discipline

P2.problem: Semantic classification (alpha_classifier: 550 calls, evidence_stance_classifier: 33 calls) dominates ~74% of run wall-clock time.
P2.user_impact: Long live-run latency; only relevant if LIVE_FULL_RESEARCH demo mode is used.
P2.semantic_risk: MEDIUM if implemented carelessly (could change which/how many claims qualify); NONE if a byte-identical-output caching layer

P2.problem: No progressive rendering -- results appear only after full assembly rather than streaming in as scoring completes.
P2.user_impact: Minor polish; current progress UX is already good enough that this is low priority.

recommended_first_implementation_slice.title: Structured top-level result summary on the primary Research results page
recommended_first_implementation_slice.description: Render the Alpha list, dominant Alpha (if any), and main conflict (if any) directly on ResearchRunPage.tsx using data that is already fetched into the `research` object but currently unrendered there (per the frontend audit finding) -- rather than requiring navigation to the separate Structure Graph / Conflict Radar tabs to see them.
recommended_first_implementation_slice.why_this_one: Directly fixes the single biggest first-impression clarity gap (P1-1), uses data the frontend already has in memory, is entirely frontend/PRESENTATION_ONLY, requires no backend or taxonomy change, requires no Provider rerun, and can be fully tested locally against the existing NVDA/QQQ/SNDK persisted runs.
likely_files: possibly extracting a shared AlphaSummaryList/MainConflictCard subcomponent reused from StructureGraphPage.tsx/ConflictRadarPage.tsx
recommended_first_implementation_slice.caveat: This slice does not address the P0 DB-availability gap -- that should be investigated/resolved in parallel (or first) since it affects whether any of these three tickers can even be opened live via the UI/API today.
